intro: AI news today centers on safety and trust failures at major platforms, a sharp market retreat from the AI trade, and incremental model releases from Google and a lesser-known lab.

stories.title: Claude Code sends your email address to websites
stories.what_happened: A widely upvoted GitHub bug report reveals that Anthropic's Claude Code agent was sending users' email addresses to arbitrary third-party websites via the User-Agent header during web searches, without explicit permission. The reporter says this behavior generated spam and scam emails and was not clearly disclosed as an opt-in/opt-out setting. The issue reportedly pushed at least one user to migrate away from Claude Code to alternative tooling.
stories.why_it_matters: As coding agents gain more autonomous web-browsing capability, silent data leakage through request metadata becomes a systemic privacy risk rather than an edge case. This incident highlights how agentic AI tools can expose personal identifiers to unknown third parties while performing routine tasks, undermining trust in AI coding assistants at a moment when enterprises are rapidly adopting them for sensitive workflows.
stories.watch_next: Watch for Anthropic's official response and whether other agentic coding tools (Cursor, Copilot, OpenRouter-based agents) are audited for similar header-leakage issues.
stories.summary: A widely upvoted GitHub bug report reveals that Anthropic's Claude Code agent was sending users' email addresses to arbitrary third-party websites via the User-Agent header during web searches, without explicit permission. The reporter says this behavior generated spam and scam emails and was not clearly disclosed as an opt-in/opt-out setting. The issue reportedly pushed at least one user to migrate away from Claude Code to alternative tooling.

stories.title: Cuban: Facebook knowingly runs AI deepfake scam ads; docs say $16B fraud revenue
stories.what_happened: Mark Cuban alleges that Meta/Facebook has knowingly run AI-generated deepfake scam ads, citing internal documents suggesting the company earns roughly $16 billion in revenue tied to fraudulent advertising. Cuban describes receiving constant emails from victims who were deceived by fake endorsement ads, including a fabricated '$294 diabetes cure' falsely attributed to him.
stories.why_it_matters: The allegation implicates one of the world's largest ad platforms in deliberately monetizing AI-generated fraud at scale, raising the stakes for platform liability as generative AI makes deepfake scam ads cheaper and more convincing to produce. If substantiated, this could trigger regulatory scrutiny and advertiser backlash similar to past content-moderation controversies, and adds pressure on Meta amid broader AI-trust concerns.
stories.watch_next: Watch for Meta's formal response, any FTC or congressional inquiry, and whether other celebrities or regulators push for mandatory ad-verification systems targeting AI-generated content.
stories.summary: Mark Cuban alleges that Meta/Facebook has knowingly run AI-generated deepfake scam ads, citing internal documents suggesting the company earns roughly $16 billion in revenue tied to fraudulent advertising. Cuban describes receiving constant emails from victims who were deceived by fake endorsement ads, including a fabricated '$294 diabetes cure' falsely attributed to him.

stories.title: Nasdaq plummets 4% into correction territory
stories.what_happened: The Nasdaq fell 5.52% to 24,315, sliding into correction territory as the S&P 500 dropped 4.36% and the Dow lost over 1,800 points. The selloff reversed post-midterm election gains and was driven by investor fears of a slowdown in AI-related data-center buildout spending.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a direct market signal that confidence in the AI capex supercycle is cracking, with investors reassessing the sustainability of massive infrastructure spending by hyperscalers and chipmakers. Given how concentrated major indices have become in AI-linked stocks, continued volatility could tighten capital availability for AI infrastructure projects and pressure valuations across the sector.
stories.watch_next: Watch upcoming earnings and capex guidance from major cloud and chip companies, and whether the selloff triggers broader reconsideration of AI infrastructure financing commitments.
stories.summary: The Nasdaq fell 5.52% to 24,315, sliding into correction territory as the S&P 500 dropped 4.36% and the Dow lost over 1,800 points. The selloff reversed post-midterm election gains and was driven by investor fears of a slowdown in AI-related data-center buildout spending.

stories.title: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash
stories.what_happened: Google rolled out Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash, a video generation model now generally available via the Gemini API and for business customers. The update adds native 15-second video creation, multi-turn conversational editing, improved reference-following, and a 30% price cut to $0.07 per second for 720p video.
stories.why_it_matters: Longer native video generation combined with cheaper per-second pricing signals Google's push to make generative video commercially viable at scale, intensifying competition with OpenAI's Sora and other video-gen entrants. The conversational multi-turn editing feature also points toward video generation becoming an iterative creative workflow rather than single-shot output, which could accelerate adoption in marketing and content production.
stories.watch_next: Watch for competitive responses from OpenAI and Runway, and how quickly enterprise adoption of API-based video generation scales given the new pricing.
stories.summary: Google rolled out Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash, a video generation model now generally available via the Gemini API and for business customers. The update adds native 15-second video creation, multi-turn conversational editing, improved reference-following, and a 30% price cut to $0.07 per second for 720p video.

stories.title: Inkling 2 Small
stories.what_happened: A new AI lab introduced Inkling 2 Small, a mixture-of-experts model with 594B total parameters and 17B active parameters, supporting image inputs and variable inference effort. The model scores 31 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, surpassing the lab's previous generation on agentic coding, vision, knowledge work, and reasoning benchmarks.
stories.why_it_matters: The release adds another capable MoE model to a crowded field of frontier-adjacent contenders, reflecting how efficient MoE architectures and large unified RL training runs continue to push benchmark performance even outside the largest labs. It underscores how quickly mid-tier AI developers are closing capability gaps with major players using efficient training techniques rather than raw scale alone.
stories.watch_next: Watch for independent benchmarking of Inkling 2 Small against established models like GPT and Gemini variants, and whether the lab releases open weights or keeps the model API-only.
